headline: At six levels the css-prop fold still renders and ships exactly what it did at one (0.517 ms/1k, 2.66 kB), while every lane that merges classes at render, atomic or runtime, has doubled or worse.

microbench.why: Six levels is where the two ways of composing separate. The css-prop fold concatenates the chain into a single class and holds 0.517 ms/1k, unchanged from one level and within noise of `vanilla`'s 0.503, while the styled fold's perf runtime collapses the `Yak → Yak` chain and holds 0.698. The atomic lanes pay per level: `bamboo` runs six `cx()` joins and emits 32 class tokens per element for 1.12 ms/1k against its own 0.508 at depth one, `stylex-layers` 1.36 through `styleq`, `panda` 17.8 re-resolving six objects. The 9.6.0 runtime at 5.07 ms/1k is what one React component per level costs.

autocannon.why: The concatenated class serves 1543 req/s at six levels, the same as at one, and `vanilla` 1473. `bamboo` (562) and `stylex-layers` (606) roughly halve from their depth-one figures. `panda` at 53 req/s is the floor and `tailwind-merge` at 345 pays six merge calls per element.

attribution.why: `next-yak-css-9.7` renders in 0.651 ms with a 0.267 ms library slice and no per-level work, against `vanilla`'s 0.631. `panda` puts 20.9 of its 22.3 ms into component self-time, 568 ms of a 608 ms JS window inside its own package. `bamboo`'s cost surfaces where its API lives: `styled-system`, the `cx` join, appears at 1.29 ms and its own package at 11.5 ms of a 39.6 ms window, six joins per instance, and `stylex-layers` shows the same shape through `@stylexjs/stylex` at 4.50 ms.

hydrate.why: Depth does not reach hydration for a static sheet: 48.4-50.0 ms across the extracted lanes with no style or layout inside the span. `panda` (126 ms) re-resolves six objects per element on the client and `goober` (117 ms) injects. The extracted cluster is one measurement.

inp.why: A single re-render through six levels costs 0.43-0.66 ms of JS in the build-time lanes, which land between 6.5 and 8.6 ms. `panda` is the exception at 61.3 ms, re-resolving six merged objects for every element in the subtree it re-renders. `goober` (23.5 ms) and `emotion` (12.0 ms) re-hash the same way.

mount.why: Cold mount at six levels sorts by work before first paint: the concatenated-class lane and `vanilla` at 72.7-74.4 ms, the atomic lanes at 83.3-87.2 as the browser matches 32 class tokens per element, `panda` at 155 ms resolving them. `emotion` and `goober` both mount at 117 ms.

renderTiming.why: One recalculation and one layout per lane, with the recalc at 0.122-0.191 ms. Thirty-two class tokens per element cost the selector matcher time inside that single recalc rather than buying extra ones.

payload.why: Payload is the clearest depth signal. The css-prop fold ships 2.66 kB gzipped at six levels, the same as at one, because six levels of rules collapse into one class name. `bamboo` grows 4.94 to 5.61 kB and `stylex-layers` 5.62 to 5.86 as each level adds tokens to the attribute, while the styled fold grows 3.79 to 4.06 kB keeping one class per level.

nsweep.why: At 4000 six-level instances the concatenated class holds 2.17 ms against `vanilla`'s 2.07 and the styled fold 2.82. `bamboo` (4.77 ms) and `stylex-layers` (5.44 ms) carry six merges per instance into the sweep. `panda` reaches 73.7 ms and `tailwind-merge` 9.93.

crossCase: The deep end of the composition ladder (the Examples `compose-1` and `compose-3` above). The css-prop fold is flat across all three depths (0.522, 0.517, 0.517 ms/1k) and so is its payload (2.67, 2.66, 2.66 kB); the styled fold's perf runtime holds too, 0.448 to 0.698. Depth is what the atomic lanes pay: `bamboo` 0.508 to 1.12 ms/1k and `stylex-layers` 0.530 to 1.36, one merge and one class token per level.
